what_this_is: Failed tasks whose cause has since been fixed, so a resubmission is not a repeat
of the same crash. failed_tasks.py prints a resubmission line for a FAILED task
ONLY when its cause appears here AND the commit named below is an ancestor of the
HEAD of the checkout the tool runs in. On the cluster that checkout is what the
jobs run, so the claim 'the cause is fixed' is checked against the code rather
than asserted in a document. A commit that is not there prints a refusal, not a
Fields. `commit` is the fix. `proof` is the command that demonstrates it and needs
no cluster. `error_matches` are substrings of the log's last error; a task whose
log IS readable is matched on those alone, so a task that died on something else
is never swept in by its position in the array. `task_rule` is used ONLY when the
log cannot be read, which is the case on a laptop and where a rebuilt script

fixed_causes.what: Methane, ammonia and water each carry one Morgan substructure, and it occurs in exactly one molecule, so none of them can reach a top-1024 chosen by how often a substructure appears in training. Their Sort & Slice vector is all zeros and the featuriser guard refuses to train on a molecule with no features.
fixed_causes.fix: Those three are dropped from every representation, found by the property rather than by name, after the shuffle and the split, so nothing already on disk changes.
error_matches: Sort & Slice produced an all-zero count vector
Sort & Slice produced a molecule with no enumerable substructures

task_rule.why: The generated script picks the representation with REPS[i % n_rep] (slurm_scripts_qm9_rerun/generate_scripts.py, the `rep=` line), so the tasks this cause touches are every index whose remainder is Sort & Slice's position in REPS. The position is read off the generated script where it is on disk; the two numbers below are used only when it is not, and they are the six representations in their generated order with Sort & Slice last.
